references.text: The priest shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the same ritual action as in Leviticus 17:6.
The blood is sprinkled around on the altar as part of the peace offering ritual, corresponding to the blood sprinkling described in Leviticus 17:6.
The fat is burned on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, the same practice mentioned in Leviticus 17:6.
The fat is burned on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, parallel to the burning of the fat in Leviticus 17:6.
The ram is burned as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, a burnt offering; the same expression is used in Leviticus 17:6.
The blood shall be sprinkled on the altar and the fat burned as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, directly parallel to Leviticus 17:6.
Blood shall be sprinkled on the altar in Ezekiel's temple vision, a continuation of the same sacrificial practice.
The book of Hebrews refers to the blood sprinkling in the tabernacle and emphasizes that almost everything is cleansed with blood under the law.
The book of Hebrews compares Jesus' sacrifice with the Old Testament offerings where the blood was brought into the sanctuary.
